panels.rationale: Single-panel H&E histopathology from a skin biopsy of a patient with confirmed gestational pemphigoid (second-trimester pregnancy case report). The caption and in-text explicitly attribute the spongiosis to the pemphigoid gestationis biopsy workup, and the visible epidermal spongiosis with dense eosinophil-rich inflammatory infiltrate and early subepidermal clefting matches the vocabulary finding 'Subepidermal blister with eosinophils' (synonym: eosinophilic spongiosis with dermal edema). Real patient-derived histology, not a diagram, control, or other-disease panel; no third-party restriction. Histology showing spongiosis with eosinophils is a classic, textbook feature of pemphigig gestationis; the 'rare' designation in the article title refers to the second-trimester presentation, not this histology. Skin tone not assessable on a histology slide; ethnicity not stated; age inferred as adult from documented pregnancy in the in-text.

Palmar involvement represents a variant distribution of the extremities bullous eruption characteristic of pemphigoid gestationis. Skin tone is dark (Fitzpatrick V-VI). No ethnicity or age stated in caption or in-text mentions.
